items.title: Carmelle bags first-ever Eurovision Asia crown
items.description: With her high-energy performance of 'Sobra-Sobra,' Filipina singer Carmelle Collado tops the jury and fan votes to win the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia

items.title: Satisfaction with Marcos government drops anew – SWS
items.description: Public satisfaction with the Marcos administration dropped anew in the third quarter survey conducted by Social Weather Stations.

items.title: Rubio to accompany Trump in Manila
items.description: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio will accompany US President Donald Trump when the latter attends the Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit in Manila on Nov. 17.

items.title: Diplomats convene ahead of ASEAN meet
items.description: Top diplomats of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations convened yesterday to prepare for the opening of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits today.

items.title: ASEAN ministers sign digital economy pact
items.description: Ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) yesterday signed the Digital Economy Framework Agreement, a priority deliverable under the Philippines’ ASEAN chairship.

items.title: Callamard returning to Philippines to meet drug war victims
items.description: Former United Nations special rapporteur on extrajudicial killings Agnès Callamard will return to the Philippines for the first time since 2017 to meet with victims of the Duterte administration’s bloody war on drugs.

items.title: Experts weigh in on Pax Silica opportunities, costs
items.description: Experts from the University of the Philippines shared their perspectives on the proposed Pax Silica initiative, examining its potential implications for the Philippines to better understand what it could mean for the country.

items.title: Pinoys find VP’s business interests ‘unacceptable’
items.description: Half of adult Filipinos are against Vice President Sara Duterte owning businesses or holding business interests while in office, according to a survey conducted by research firm Momentum.

items.title: ASEAN souvenir shop makes P500,000 on 1st day
items.description: The Department of Tourism generated around P500,000 in souvenir sales from Filipino micro, small and medium enterprises in the cultural and creative industries at the 49th ASEAN International Media Center on Friday.

items.title: Philippines to deepen ties with Brazil on energy, agriculture
items.description: The Philippines is eyeing to deepen ties with Brazil in a number of key areas, including energy, agriculture and food security, as it strives to mitigate the impact of the El Niño phenomenon.

items.title: CICC identifies hackers in government data breach
items.description: Cybersecurity officials have identified some of the hackers who were involved in a massive wave of data breaches, which targeted 23 national government agencies and other institutions.

items.title: LIVE UPDATES: 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila
items.description: Leaders and representatives of the 11 members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, and their allies, are gathering in Manila for the bloc's biggest event of the year

items.title: From micro to massive, ASEAN’s entrepreneurs face regulatory hurdles
items.description: ‘It's incredibly frustrating that even the simplest of ideas seem to have a lot of difficulty getting implemented,’ former CIMB chairman Nazir Razak says, criticizing ASEAN’s slow progress toward economic integration

items.title: Thousands of students protest vs Pax Silica, Trump’s arrival in Manila
items.description: More groups are expected to stage protests across the country in the coming days, coinciding with the ASEAN Summit

items.title: 5 Philippine creative cities team up to make UNESCO badge count
items.description: Baguio, Cebu, Iloilo, Dumaguete, and Quezon City hope to turn global recognition into real support for local artists, educators, and communities

items.title: Lula: Philippine state visit start of ‘new age of relations’ with Brazil
items.description: 'A new age not just trade-wise but also a new age in politics as we have very common ideas and thoughts in relation to the need for reforming the UN, in advocating for multilateralism,' says Brazilian President Lula
